req.title: Support all HTTP verbs on /status/<code>
req.statement: The system shall accept GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, HEAD, OPTIONS, and TRACE on /status/<code>.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that /status/<code> must accept GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, HEAD, OPTIONS, and TRACE. The source shows the route is registered for GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH, TRACE (not HEAD or OPTIONS explicitly, but Flask handles HEAD automatically for GET routes). Tests must cover: (1) positive - each supported verb returns the requested status code exactly; (2) negative - invalid/non-numeric codes return 400; (3) boundary - status codes at numeric boundaries (100, 200, 400, 500, 599). Mutation resilience requires exact status code assertions, both sides of conditionals, and coverage of the ValueError path in the source.

tests.name: test_all_verbs_return_correct_status_codes
actions: Send GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE each to /status/200 and /status/404
expected: Each verb returns exactly the requested status code
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_all_verbs_return_correct_status_codes():
    methods = [
        ('get', client.get),
        ('post', client.post),
        ('put', client.put),
        ('patch', client.patch),
        ('delete', client.delete),
    ]
    for code in [200, 404]:
        for name, method in methods:
            r = method(f'/status/{code}')
            assert r.status_code == code, f"{name} /status/{code} got {r.status_code}"

test_all_verbs_return_correct_status_codes()
